[2024 fall ms applied — problem 4]

Multiple regression of $Y$ on $X_1, X_2, X_3$, $n = 25$, SS(Total) $= 248.0$; table of SSReg for all predictor subsets (SSReg($X_1,X_2,X_3) = 181.8$, SSReg($X_1,X_2) = 145.2$, etc.), $\alpha = 0.05$. (1) Global F-test of $H_0: \beta_1=\beta_2=\beta_3=0$. (2) Compute the extra SSReg$(X_3\mid X_1,X_2)$. (3) Test whether $X_3$ can be dropped. (4) Write the first row of the reduced-model $X$-matrix testing $H_0: \beta_2 = \beta_3 = 0$ (first obs: $Y=10, X_1=1985, X_2=59.7, X_3=2205$).

- MS(Error) = SS(Error)/df(Error) = 66.2/21 ≈ 3.1524

- F₀.₀₅(3, 21) ≈ 3.07

Since the test statistic exceeds the critical value, I reject H₀ and conclude the full model is statistically significant.

## (2) Extra SS(X₃ | X₁, X₂)

This represents the marginal contribution of X₃ when X₁ and X₂ are already in the model. The extra sum of squares is calculated as the difference between the full model and the reduced model without X₃.

SS(X₃ | X₁, X₂) = SSReg(X₁, X₂, X₃) - SSReg(X₁, X₂) = 181.8 - 145.2 = 36.6

The test statistic is F = [SS(X₃ | X₁, X₂) / 1] / MS(Error) = [36.6 / 1] /
(66.2/21) = 36.6 / 3.1524 ≈ 11.60

Comparing to the critical value F₀.₀₅(1, 21) ≈ 4.32, since 11.60 > 4.32, I reject H₀ and conclude that X₃ is statistically significant and should be retained.

# Solution: Multiple Regression Analysis

## (1) Global F-Test: H₀: β₁ = β₂ = β₃ = 0

**ANOVA Decomposition:**
$$\text{SS(Error)} = \text{SS(Total)} - \text{SSReg}(X_1,X_2,X_3) = 248.0 - 181.8 = 66.2$$

**Degrees of freedom:**
- df(Reg) = 3 (number of predictors)
- df(Error) = n - p = 25 - 4 = 21 (p = 4 includes intercept)

**Mean Squares:**
$$\text{MS(Reg)} = \frac{181.8}{3} = 60.6$$
$$\text{MS(Error)} = \frac{66.2}{21} = 3.152$$

**F-statistic:**
$$F = \frac{\text{MS(Reg)}}{\text{MS(Error)}} = \frac{60.6}{3.152} = 19.21$$

**Critical value:** $F_{0.05}(3, 21) \approx 3.07$

**Conclusion:** Since $F = 19.21 > 3.07$, **reject H₀**. The full model is highly significant at α = 0.05.

---

## (2) Extra Sum of Squares for X₃

Using the principle of sequential SS:
$$\text{SS}(X_3 \mid X_1, X_2) = \text{SSReg}(X_1,X_2,X_3) - \text{SSReg}(X_1,X_2)$$
$$= 181.8 - 145.2 = \boxed{36.6}$$

This represents the additional reduction in sum of squares when X₃ is added to the model already containing X₁ and X₂.

---

## (3) Partial F-Test: Can X₃ be dropped?

**Hypothesis:** H₀: β₃ = 0 (vs. H₁: β₃ ≠ 0)

**Partial F-statistic:**
$$F = \frac{\text{SS}(X_3 \mid X_1, X_2) / 1}{\text{MS(Error)}} = \frac{36.6}{3.152} = 11.60$$

**Critical value:** $F_{0.05}(1, 21) \approx 4.32$

**Conclusion:** Since $F = 11.60 > 4.32$, **reject H₀**. **X₃ cannot be dropped**; it makes a statistically significant contribution to the model even after accounting for X₁ and X₂.

---

## (4) First Row of Reduced-Model X-Matrix for H₀: β₂ = β₃ = 0

When testing H₀: β₂ = β₃ = 0, the **reduced model** contains only the intercept and X₁:
$$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \varepsilon$$

The reduced-model design matrix has the structure [1 | X₁].

For the first observation (Y = 10, X₁ = 1985, X₂ = 59.7, X₃ = 2205):

$$\boxed{\text{First row of } X_{\text{reduced}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1985 \end{bmatrix}}$$

Where:
- First column = 1 (intercept)
- Second column = 1985 (value of X₁ for first observation)

Note: X₂ and X₃ are excluded because they correspond to parameters being tested (H₀: β₂ = β₃ = 0).
